title:
The Neutrino as an Open Helical Two-Photon State:
Mass Scale, Helicity, and Tetrahedral Leading-Order Mixing
content: Within Delta-c Mechanics the neutrino is proposed to be the same two-photon system as the electron, distinguished by orbital topology: the electron occupies a closed circular orbit, the neutrino an open helix. Its spin-½ representation is the pair spinor of the companion Clifford-algebra paper with mass parameter mν; the single-helicity limit is a boost along the spin axis, one chiral sector carrying the particle and the other suppressed as mν²/4E. Open (O7) are the identification of the open-orbit dynamics with that spinor and the Majorana condition, undecidable at the single-particle level; exchange statistics are inherited from the spin-statistics theorem. Beta decay is recast as pair production: the Q-value creates the electron’s closed orbit while the pre-existing nuclear pair reorganises into the helix. The Coulomb coupling of the pair to the proton at the inverse-coupling length, with the open-insertion suppression, gives a conditional mass scale mν = mₑgₐ²α³/2π = 31.7 meV (O4), within 5–10% of the degenerate pair of the oscillation spectrum. The three mass eigenstates are placed at the lower vertices of a regular tetrahedron, giving tribimaximal mixing at leading order and, from one measured input, the solar angle and splitting; the ratio m₃ = 2m₁ and normal ordering follow if the μ–τ-odd mode, the one with no electron overlap, is the uncoupled and heaviest mode, a mechanism motivated by the framework’s half-cycle engagement filter and not yet derived (O8). The open helix has no closure-frozen duality angle, so the framework supplies no second configuration for the antiparticle; this motivates Majorana character without deriving it, with ⟨mββ⟩ = 8–30 meV under the tetrahedral spectrum if it holds. Exposures: the input-free ratio Δm²₃₁/Δm²₂₁ = 3/√α = 35.12 stands 2.3σ above the JUNO 2026 value 33.96 ± 0.50, the test most likely to fail; the spectrum sum Σm = 116.9 meV is excluded by DESI DR2 with the CMB under ΛCDM, surviving only under dynamical dark energy; the solar-angle relation sin²θ₁₂ = (1 − 12α)/3 agrees at +0.1σ but its coefficient is not derived; the reactor angle is not reproduced (O2).
